scope: Streaming authenticated backup encryption codec only; not a usable backup/restore operation

format.keyWrapping: AES-256-GCM under a caller-supplied 32-byte backup key; 12-byte random nonce and 16-byte tag
format.segmentAuthentication: AES-256-GCM with a 12-byte nonce containing the sequential 64-bit frame index; 16-byte tags. Associated data binds the complete header hash, frame index and plaintext length.
format.completion: Required authenticated zero-length frame at the next index; trailing bytes are rejected.

verifiedBehavior: Empty, one-byte, exact-segment and multisegment streams round trip through nonseekable fragmented readers.
Every encrypted archive gets a fresh data key and identifier.
Header, wrapping nonce, wrapped key, tags, ciphertext and completion tampering are rejected.
Wrong keys fail before any plaintext is emitted; data from a failing frame is not emitted.
Truncation, dropped final frames, reordered, duplicated, omitted, foreign frames and trailing bytes are rejected.
Invalid lengths are rejected before input-driven allocation.
A 32-MiB generated input uses at most 1-MiB read/write requests and the implementation retains two fixed 1-MiB working buffers.
Cancellation before output and after a complete data frame does not create a valid completed archive.
limitations: The codec has not yet been connected to snapshot creation, manifest generation/verification, atomic archive publication, retention rotation, HTTP/CLI commands or restore.
A decoder can emit an authenticated prefix before discovering a later corruption. Callers must keep all output in private staging until full archive authentication and manifest verification finish.
No production archive or secret key was created, read or changed.
No independent cryptographic audit or full backup-under-sustained-edits acceptance is claimed.
